column1: # Shared parity vectors: decore::gradeOffsets, gradePolicyOf and
# hasDurability (src/domain/ItemGrade.h). Every row is asserted for exact
# equality by the server's formula_tests and by the client's decore_tests
# on every client toolchain. A changed expected value is a balance change:
# review it as one. UPDATE_GOLDENS=1 formula_tests rewrites the expected
# Tab-separated, one row per call: function, row name, the inputs, and the
# expected result last. A policy is written by its enumerator name (None,
# Plain, Weapon, Cloth, Grocery, Accessory); an item class by its wire id.
# gradeOffsets columns: policy grade expected, where expected is the six
#   offsets comma-separated in GradeOffsets order: durability, damage,
#   critical, defense, protection, luck. Every policy is pinned at grades
#   -5, -1 (the grade an item without one reads), 0 to 11 and 20, which
#   covers each side of grade 4, both far ends of each linear formula and
#   the grocery protection's half step: (grade - 4) / 2 truncates toward
#   zero, so grades 3 and 5 move nothing, grades 1 and 2 move -1 and grade
# gradePolicyOf columns: itemClass expected policy. One row per wire class
#   0-89, named after the class, plus one id on each side of the table.
# hasDurability columns: itemClass expected (0 or 1). The same rows.
# The per-class rows are the server's own choices, oddities included:
# CoreZap is Plain (a grade that moves nothing) and keeps no durability;
# ShoulderArmor, Persona, Fascia and Mitten are Grocery; Dermis, Fascia,
# CarryingReceiver, CoreZap and VampireAmulet keep no durability. Classes
# the server does not build on ConcreteItem are None and 0.
